However, preliminary evidence of their efficacy is conflicting,16 and further large controlled studies are considered warrant- ed.2,15 Systemic antineoplastic therapy should also be given if the primary tumour is chemosensitive. Endocrine treatment is usually preferred for patients with breast and prostatic can- cers, and can produce useful control of symptoms from bone metastases.1,2 Patients who also have visceral metas- tases or who have hormone resistant tumours should prob- ably be treated with cytotoxic antineoplastics.2 New drugs under investigation include denosumab and at- rasentan.11 1.
